canonical_definition:
Space of definitions. The available usage treats forward reaction prediction as determining the potential products of a chemical reaction from a given set of reactants and reagents. The definition and source text use the same framing, describing it as the "proactive determination of potential products" from those inputs.

Variants. It appears alongside other molecular instruction tasks, including molecule description generation, molecular property prediction, IUPAC name generation, and retrosynthesis. The papers shown here do not name sub-variants, domains, modalities, or alternative formulations of forward reaction prediction itself.

Space of elicitation and scores. No paper records a measured_by instrument for this behavior. Papers link it to a single instrument, Mol-Instructions, and that recorded link is causal rather than measured_by: the paper says Mol-Instructions equips LLMs with new insights into chemical reaction prediction, and presents it as an instruction dataset.

What it is taken as evidence of. Papers do not link forward reaction prediction to any construct, so the available material does not specify what broader property it is taken to evidence.

Mol-Instructions: A Large-Scale Biomolecular Instruction Dataset for Large Language Models
Hierarchical Graph Tokenization for Molecule-Language Alignment
LLaMo: Large Language Model-based Molecular Graph Assistant
